zh.principle: **协议**：SSH 1.x（Secure Shell (SSH) Protocol Version 1.x）。SSH 1.x 的地位由新文档的回溯描述确定：RFC 4253 §5 写明「Earlier versions of this protocol have not been formally documented, but it is widely known that they use 'protoversion' of “1.x” (e.g., “1.5” or “1.3”).」它是一条存在过但没有正式标准化文本的旧协议线。
zh.why: 2.0 重写的理由写在架构文档摘要里：「The SSH protocol consists of three major components: The Transport Layer Protocol provides server authentication, confidentiality, and integrity with perfect forward secrecy.」架构文档把前向保密描述为 2.0 传输层提供的属性，而旧协议线没有对应的标准化描述可依据。
zh.used: §5 把适用范围收窄：「Information in this section is only relevant for implementations supporting compatibility with SSH versions 1.x.」兼容做法由新服务器让步：§5.1 的小标题即 Old Client, New Server，规定「the server SHOULD identify its 'protoversion' as “1.99”.」并要求使用 2.0 的客户端把它认作与 2.0 等同。
zh.broken: 文档缺失与兼容过程本身都是问题：§5 说「the only known documentation of the 1.x protocol is contained in README files that are shipped along with the source code [ssh-1.2.30].」；§5.2 说明新客户端可能先发数据，于是「the old protocol may already be corrupt when the client learns that the server is old」，此时应关闭连接并按旧协议重连。
zh.history:
RFC 4253 与 RFC 4251 同为 2006 年 1 月的 Standards Track 文档（署名 T.Ylonen，SSH Communications Security Corp，与 C.Lonvick, Ed.，Cisco Systems），头部都没有 Obsoletes 或 Updates 行；§5 记录当时的现实——许多实现已用 2.0，「but it is known that there are still devices using the previous versions」。

**技术参数与复算边界**

该条目的形式模型是 \(\mathrm{Adv}^{\Pi}_A(\lambda)\le n\cdot\mathrm{Adv}^{\mathrm{prf}}_F(\lambda)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{aead}}(\lambda)\)。输入：输入：SSH 1.x的公开参数、密钥/随机数与消息；变量说明：Π 协议，A 敌手，n 会话数，PRF/AEAD 为底层原语。 预期输出：按 SSH 1.x 的规范执行后得到可验证的输出或可比较的优势界。 复算必须给出输入、步骤、输出和单位；示例只演示流程，不替代标准测试向量。

复杂度由密钥长度、分组/状态规模、轮数、随机数质量和敌手模型共同决定；参数越界、版本差异与实现侧信道都可能使公式结论失效。已登记限制：该条目只给出形式模型与可复算步骤，不声称已完成生产实现、侧信道认证或第三方安全评估。

**参数与状态规模**

公式 \(\mathrm{Adv}^{\Pi}_A(\lambda)\le n\cdot\mathrm{Adv}^{\mathrm{prf}}_F(\lambda)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{aead}}(\lambda)\) 的输入、输出和单位必须逐项登记；复算顺序为：1. 把协议消息序列写成状态机 2. 用混合论证逐个替换原语 3. 把剩余优势归约到 PRF/AEAD 安全。

状态规模、密钥长度、分组长度和轮数决定复杂度；这些量不能从标题推断，必须以标准或实现文档为准。

en.principle: **Protocol**: Secure Shell (SSH) Protocol Version 1.x (SSH 1.x). The status of SSH 1.x is set by the retrospective description in the newer documents: RFC 4253 §5 says "Earlier versions of this protocol have not been formally documented, but it is widely known that they use 'protoversion' of “1.x” (e.g., “1.5” or “1.3”)." It is a protocol line that existed without a standardised text.
en.why: The reason for the 2.0 rewrite is in the architecture document's abstract: "The SSH protocol consists of three major components: The Transport Layer Protocol provides server authentication, confidentiality, and integrity with perfect forward secrecy." The architecture abstract presents forward secrecy as a property the 2.0 transport layer provides, and the older line has no standardised description to lean on.
en.used:
Section 5 narrows its own scope: "Information in this section is only relevant for implementations supporting compatibility with SSH versions 1.x." The compatibility trick is a version string the newer server offers to older clients (§5.1, headed Old Client, New Server): it says "the server SHOULD identify its 'protoversion' as “1.99”." and requires clients on protocol 2.0 to treat that value as identical to 2.0.

A shared name may belong to an algorithm, standard, event, person or term; this entry is responsible only for its catalogue binding and does not absorb adjacent records. If versions, regions or institutions define the name differently, the differences stay side by side.
en.broken: Both the missing documentation and the compatibility procedure are problems: §5 records that "the only known documentation of the 1.x protocol is contained in README files that are shipped along with the source code [ssh-1.2.30]." and §5.2 notes a new client may send data first, so "the old protocol may already be corrupt when the client learns that the server is old", after which it should close and reconnect under the old protocol.
en.history: RFC 4253 and RFC 4251 are both January 2006 Standards Track publications (signed T. Ylonen, SSH Communications Security Corp, and C. Lonvick, Ed., Cisco Systems) with no Obsoletes or Updates line; §5 records the reality of the time — many implementations used 2.0, "but it is known that there are still devices using the previous versions".

zh: 识别串：连接开头明文交换的版本与软件说明行。
1.x：没有正式标准化文本的旧 SSH 协议线。
1.99：双支持服务器用来表明兼容的版本串。
ssh-1.2.30：旧协议唯一的非正式材料来源。
回退重连：发现对端是旧协议时的处置。
en: Identification string: the cleartext version and software line sent first.
protoversion: the version field inside that string.
1.x: the older SSH line with no standardised text.
1.99: the version string a dual-supporting server announces.
ssh-1.2.30: the only informal source for the old protocol.
Fall back and reconnect: the handling when the peer turns out to be old.
